paragraphs: Rav Acha Sar Habbirah. Rashi, Ketubbot 88a: this was his byname; at 22a he gives no explanation. He and Rav Pinchas (an error, since no mention of him is found; Yevamot 45a reads Rabbi Tanchum), son of Rabbi Chiyya of Kefar Akko, ransomed captive women; they came before Rabbi Ammi. He said an incident came before Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha in Antioch (Arakhin 22b; Ketubbot 88a omits Nappacha). He presented a ruling before the sages in Usha, Bava Batra 146a; Ketubbot 22a. Rashbam: when the Sanhedrin were exiled there. This requires examination: even on the second exile to Usha in Rabbi’s father’s days (see Rabban Gamliel the elder), how could he be in Rabbi Ammi and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha’s time? There is also Rav Acha Sar Habbirah in Tosefta, chapter 2.
